details: A proper random-counterexample strategy halves the expected version-space size.
proof: At each stage, query a hypothesis minimizing its $L_1$ distance to the pointwise average of the current version space.  For every target, a uniformly random counterexample leaves at most half the current hypotheses in expectation.  Induction and Jensen's inequality for the concave logarithm then give expected remaining query cost at most $\log|\mathcal H|$.
witness_verification: For the $n$ singletons together with the empty concept, $\log|\mathcal H|=\log(n+1)$ whereas the proper randomized equivalence-query complexity is 1.
name: Log Size / Random Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity
